description.purpose: Search Slack messages, channels, and users by free-text query and return ranked smart IDs.
when_to_use: When the user wants to find a message by partial text or sender.
When locating a channel by partial name or topic without knowing the exact id.
when_not_to_use: When the channel id is already known and you want every message — use `list_objects` with `collection=<channel_id>`.
When the user id is already known — use `fetch` with the smart user ID.
limitations: Returns at most 25 results per call (Slack search.messages cap with cursor).
Search index lag of up to 60s for newly posted messages.
Free-tier workspaces only retain 90 days of message history searchable.
description.parameter_overview: Single `query` string supporting Slack search modifiers (e.g. `from:@alice in:#general`); ranked results returned as smart IDs of the form slack-prod-slack:object:Message:C0123:1700000000.000100 or slack-prod-slack:object:Channel:C0123.

query.description: Free-text search query, optionally with Slack search modifiers (`from:`, `in:`, `before:`, `after:`).

truncation.guidance_template: Showing {N} of {Total} matches. Use `cursor` to paginate or refine your query (e.g. add `from:@user` modifier).

description.purpose: Fetch the full Slack object addressed by a smart ID (Message, Channel, or User).
when_to_use: When you have a smart ID returned by `search` or `list_objects`.
When you need the full message blocks, channel topic, or user profile.
limitations: Message blocks may be large — request without blocks via `properties` projection if size matters.
Returns 404 (not_found) if the message was deleted, the channel archived, or the user deactivated.
description.parameter_overview: Single `id` string in the smart-ID format `slack-prod-slack:object:{Message|Channel|User}:{slack_id}`; for Message the slack_id encodes both channel and timestamp (`C0123:1700000000.000100`).

truncation.guidance_template: Object exceeded {threshold} tokens; {N} fields included. Re-call with `properties` projection (drop `blocks` for very long messages).

description.purpose: List the Slack channels (public + private the bot is in) and DMs the integration has access to.
when_to_use: At session start to discover what channels the bot can read.
When mapping a free-text request to a specific channel id.
limitations: Only channels the bot is a member of are visible (private channels require explicit invite).
Returns metadata only — use `list_objects` to enumerate messages within a channel.
description.parameter_overview: Optional `pattern` (glob on channel name) and `types` (csv: public_channel, private_channel, mpim, im); defaults return all channels and dms the bot can see.

truncation.guidance_template: Listed {N} channels. Use `pattern` to narrow by name or `types` to filter by channel kind.

description.purpose: List Slack messages within a chosen channel with time-range filter, projection, and cursor pagination.
when_to_use: When enumerating messages in a known channel.
When server-side filter by time range (`oldest`/`latest` ts) is needed.
when_not_to_use: When you have an explicit message ts — use `fetch`.
When the channel id is unknown — use `search` or `list_collections` first.
limitations: Cursor pagination only; max 1000 messages per call (Slack hard cap).
Filter expressions limited to time-range (`oldest`/`latest`); for content filters use `search`.
Sort is implicit by ts descending (newest first); cannot reverse via parameter.

truncation.guidance_template: Returned {N} of approximately {Total} messages. Use `cursor` to paginate or `properties` to project fewer fields (drop `blocks` first).

description.purpose: Create a new Slack message or edit an existing one (smart routing by message ts presence).
when_to_use: When posting a new message to a channel from an automation.
When patching the text or blocks of a previously posted message.
limitations: Cannot upsert into Channel or User — only Message objects. Use `channels_archive` or admin tools for those.
Required field on create: `data.channel` and either `data.text` or `data.blocks`.
Re-posting the same content creates a duplicate message — Slack has no deduplication on text equality.
description.parameter_overview: `collection` is the channel id. Provide `data.text` (and optional `data.blocks`) for create; `id` (channel:ts smart ID) + `data` for edit.

truncation.guidance_template: {action} succeeded for message {ts} in {channel}. Refetch with `fetch` if full payload was truncated.

description.purpose: Delete a Slack message. For channel removal use `channels_archive` instead — Slack does not allow channel deletion.
when_to_use: When removing a posted message that was sent by mistake.
When sweeping bot-posted messages older than a retention window.
limitations: Can only delete messages posted by the bot itself unless the token has `chat:write.public` admin scope.
Re-deleting an already-deleted message returns `message_not_found` (no-op via idempotent retry).
Cannot delete a Channel object — Slack only supports `channels_archive`.
description.parameter_overview: `type: 'object'` + `id` (smart ID of Message: `Message:C0123:1700000000.000100`) + `confirm: true`. Batch delete supported via `ids` array.

truncation.guidance_template: Deleted {deleted_count} of {requested} messages. Failures listed in `failed` array (most often: `message_not_found` or `cant_delete_message`).

description.purpose: Send a message to a Slack channel or DM with optional thread reply, blocks, and attachments. Distinct from `upsert`: this is the ergonomic single-purpose action for posting (no edit smart-routing overhead).
when_to_use: When the agent wants to post a one-off notification or response.
When threading a reply under a known parent message via `thread_ts`.
when_not_to_use: When editing an existing message — use `upsert` with `id`.
When sending many messages in batch — call `messages_send` per channel; Slack rate limits are per-channel.
limitations: Subject to per-channel posting rate limit (~1 message/second sustained).
Re-running with same `text` produces a duplicate (not idempotent).
`blocks` field is mutually exclusive with plain `text` for rich layout.
description.parameter_overview: Required: `channel` (channel id or `#channel-name`), one of `text` or `blocks`. Optional: `thread_ts` (parent message ts), `unfurl_links` (bool, default true), `mrkdwn` (bool, default true).

truncation.guidance_template: Message sent to {channel} at ts={ts}. Reply in thread by passing `thread_ts={ts}` on next send.

description.purpose: Edit a previously posted Slack message identified by channel+ts. Distinct from `upsert`: ergonomic single-purpose action for edits with no smart-id parsing overhead.
when_to_use: When updating the text or blocks of a previously posted message.
When marking an automation message as 'completed' by patching the body.
limitations: Can only edit messages posted by the bot itself.
Edits within 5 minutes do not show 'edited' badge; later edits do (Slack policy).
Re-applying the same edit is a no-op idempotent (Slack returns same envelope).
description.parameter_overview: Required: `channel` (channel id), `ts` (message timestamp), and one of `text` or `blocks`. Optional: `as_user` (bool).

truncation.guidance_template: Message edited at {channel}:{ts}. Re-edit with same content is no-op.

description.purpose: Archive a Slack channel (Slack's canonical removal — channels cannot be hard-deleted).
when_to_use: When closing out a project channel after completion.
When sweeping inactive channels older than a retention policy.
limitations: Re-archiving an archived channel returns `already_archived` (idempotent).
The default `#general` channel cannot be archived (Slack platform constraint).
Archived channels remain queryable via `list_collections` with `types` including archived.
description.parameter_overview: Required: `channel` (channel id). Archives the channel; members are notified by Slack platform.

description.purpose: Two-step coherent task: post a message, then post a follow-up reply in the same thread once an external trigger fires (or after a fixed delay).
when_to_use: When announcing a long-running job and threading status updates under the parent message.
When confirming an action by acknowledging immediately and updating with the result.
when_not_to_use: When the parent and follow-up are unrelated — call `messages_send` twice.
When you need more than 2 sequential messages — orchestrate via `messages_send` with `thread_ts`.
limitations: Atomicity is best-effort: if step 2 fails, the parent message remains posted (partial-failure strategy: `report`).
Delay between step 1 and step 2 capped at 30s (for longer waits, schedule externally).
Subject to per-channel posting rate limit (~1 message/second sustained).
description.parameter_overview: Coarse parameters per Pass 3 design: `channel`, `parent_text` (initial message), `followup_text` (threaded reply), and optional `delay_ms` (default 0).

truncation.guidance_template: Posted parent {parent_ts}; followup {followup_ts}. If step2_ok=false, retry with `messages_send(thread_ts=parent_ts)`.
